subject.title: fix(fal): apply request policy to provider HTTP config

question: Should Fal activate the full existing provider request-policy contract, including explicit private-network and proxy or dispatcher behavior, or should its forwarded policy be restricted?
rationale: The change makes previously ignored security-sensitive network configuration effective for existing Fal users, and the unchanged PR head contains no controlled proof establishing the intended boundary.

options.title: Honor the full policy with proof
options.body: Accept the established provider contract after adding controlled coverage for policy forwarding, default denial, explicit private-network opt-in, and header isolation.

options.title: Restrict Fal policy forwarding
options.body: Forward only the Fal-approved subset if private-network, proxy, TLS, or header controls are not intended for this provider.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave Fal’s current behavior unchanged until an owner defines and proves its provider-specific network policy.

recommendation.title: Honor the full policy with proof
recommendation.body: Accept the established provider contract after adding controlled coverage for policy forwarding, default denial, explicit private-network opt-in, and header isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged sibling-provider work supplies the closest concrete history for this request-policy and security invariant.
